ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On the first day of school, Ashley the teacher asked some of her students what their favorite color was and used those results to construct the pie chart pictured below. During this first day, $165$ students chose yellow as their favorite color. The next day, she polled $30$ additional students and was shocked when none of them chose yellow. After making a new pie chart based on the combined results of both days, Ashley noticed that the angle measure of the sector representing the students whose favorite color was yellow had decreased. Compute the difference, in degrees, between the old and the new angle measures.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The pie chart has three labeled sectors. The Red sector is marked 60°, the Blue sector is marked 210°, and the remaining sector is labeled Yellow. Reasoning: Since a full circle is 360°, the original Yellow angle is 360° - 60° - 210° = 90°. On the first day, 165 students chose yellow, so those 165 students represent 90°/360° = 1/4 of the first-day poll. Therefore the first-day total is 165 × 4 = 660 students. On the second day, 30 more students were polled and none chose yellow, so the combined total is 660 + 30 = 690 students while the yellow count remains 165. The new Yellow sector angle is 360° × 165/690 = 1980/23°. The decrease is 90° - 1980/23° = 90/23°.

method.method_draft: First describe/read the pie chart: the red sector is marked 60°, the blue sector is marked 210°, and the remaining sector is labeled Yellow. Therefore the original yellow angle is 360° - 60° - 210° = 90°. From the text, 165 first-day students chose yellow, so 165 students correspond to 90/360 = 1/4 of the first-day poll; hence the first-day total is 660. The second day adds 30 students and none chose yellow, so the combined total is 690 while yellow remains 165. The new yellow angle is 360·165/690 = 1980/23 degrees. Subtract from the old yellow angle: 90 - 1980/23 = 90/23 degrees.

method.method_draft: First read the image: the pie chart has Red = 60°, Blue = 210°, and Yellow as the leftover sector, so Yellow originally has angle 90° and all non-yellow colors together have angle 270°. Thus, on the first day, the yellow-to-non-yellow ratio is 90:270 = 1:3. Since the text says 165 students chose yellow on the first day, the first-day non-yellow count is 3·165 = 495. The next day adds 30 non-yellow students and 0 yellow students, so the new yellow-to-non-yellow count ratio is 165:(495+30) = 165:525 = 11:35. In the new pie chart, if the yellow angle is x, then x:(360-x) = 11:35. Solve 35x = 11(360-x), giving x = 1980/23°. The decrease is 90° - 1980/23° = 90/23°.
